requirement: A tool MUST also accept `node` and `data` together. Look up the existing ID and compare its stored identity with the deserialized `data` using `D::NodeData` equality. Use that ID on a match. An unassigned ID, malformed data, or a mismatch produces a tool error, even if the supplied data would be valid on its own. A `path` address may include `location` and must be used separately from `node` and `data`.
rationale:
The single marked test, `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[agent_node_addresses_round_trip_and_reject_inconsistent_identities_before_reads]`, covers each obligation in `node_reference.consistency`.

- **Consistent `node` and `data` are accepted and the ID is used.**
  - `list_sources` returns entries shaped `{node, data}`, as shown in `impl[Session/ToolSession]/fn[dispatch]`.
  - The test passes the whole `entry` to `read_node`, so the call carries both fields.
  - It asserts the resulting root page's `children`.
  - It also asserts that the `node`-only, `data`-only and `path`-only forms give the same dependencies as the combined form (`from_entry.dependencies`).
- **Mismatch is an error.** `{"node": entry["node"], "data": "parser.rs#impl[Parser]"}` pairs the file node with data that is valid on its own but belongs to a different node. The test asserts `is_err()`.
- **An unassigned ID is an error even when the data is valid.** `{"node": 10000, "data": entry["data"]}` is asserted to be an error.
- **Malformed data is an error.** `{"node": entry["node"], "data": false}` is asserted to be an error.
- **`path` is used separately from `node` and `data`.**
  - `{"path", "data"}` and `{"path", "node"}` are both rejected.
  - `path` with `location` works on its own, since the positive read of the child by `{"path", "location"}` succeeds.
  - `location` without `path` is rejected.
- **Rejected requests have no side effects.** The test asserts that the `reads` counter is unchanged after all the invalid requests, so they fail before any read.

The tests don't cover `path` combined with both `node` and `data`, or with `location` plus `node`. Those cases add no distinct condition, because `path` with either field alone is already rejected. I found no gap.
